title: Naming Body Parts and Hygiene Tools
comp: name parts of my body and the things I use to keep clean

gram.focus: Common nouns; adjectives for size and condition
box: Nouns name the things we use: soap, towel, brush, tooth.
Adjectives describe them: a soft towel, a new brush, clean hands.

mini: Draw and label one hygiene tool or body part.

sit.t: It is morning. You are going to school. Mother calls you to wash before you eat.
q: What do you use to wash?
Which parts of your body do you wash?

read.task: Read the word. Then point to the thing or the body part.

write.task: Trace and write: "soap", "hand", "tooth". Then label your drawing.

integ: Play "Simon says". Touch your nose, your hand, your tooth. Then name the tool you use for each.
rubric: name six body parts and hygiene tools
describe a tool with an adjective
label a drawing of a hygiene tool

title: Describing Healthy Routines and Foods
comp: describe healthy habits, clean food and daily routines

gram.focus: Verbs in the present; simple sentences with adjectives
box: We bathe every morning. He drinks clean water.
Adjectives go before the noun: clean water, sweet fruit.

phon.focus: Final sounds and syllables in health and food words

mini: Add one healthy habit or food phrase to the strip.

sit.t: At break time your friend eats a mango from the ground and drinks water from a dirty cup.
q: What do you say to your friend?
What is good food and clean water?

read.task: Read the phrase. Then tick the healthy one.

write.task: Write two healthy habits: "I ____ every day." "I drink ____ water."

integ: Make a healthy plate with your friend. Say: "This is rice. This is fruit. This is clean water."
rubric: describe three healthy habits
say what I eat and drink
read and spell water, fruit, bathing

title: Giving Safety Instructions and Requests
comp: give simple health instructions and ask politely about washing

box: An instruction tells somebody what to do: Wash your hands. Brush your teeth.
We ask politely with May I…? and Can I…?

phon.focus: Digraphs in hygiene actions and objects

mini: Add one polite health-related request or warning.

sit.t: Your little brother comes from playing in the dust. He wants to eat bread.
q: What do you tell him to do first?
How do you ask for the towel?

read.task: Read the instruction. Then do it with your hands.

write.task: Write two instructions for your brother. Start with "Wash…" and "Brush…".

l: Child: May I use the towel?
Mother: Wash your hands first, then eat.

integ: Give three instructions to a friend: wash, brush, comb. Your friend does the actions.
rubric: give three health instructions
ask politely about washing
read and spell brush, bath, wash

title: Reviewing Healthy Habits and Final Presentation
comp: talk about keeping clean and present my work

gram.focus: Sentence editing and verb tense review
box: he brush → He brushes. we drink water → We drink water.
With he, she, it the verb takes -s.

mini: Finalise the strip with tools, phrases, a chant and one drawing.

sit.t: Your class is preparing a clean-hands corner for the school. The teacher asks each pupil to present their Staying Clean Strip.
q: What do you do to stay clean?
Which habit will you show the class?

l: We wash our hands before eating.

i: We wash our hands before eating.
read.task: Read the sentences. Then say which one you do every day.

write.task: Write three sentences: "To stay clean, I ____, ____ and ____." Correct "he brush" first.

l: I wash my hands before I eat. (rub hands)
I brush my teeth every day. (brush motion)

integ: Present your strip in a group. Each pupil says one habit, then the group chants "Clean and strong!".
rubric: describe what I do to stay clean
correct a sentence with the verb -s
present my Staying Clean Strip

title: Naming and Talking About Games
comp: name indoor and outdoor games and the things we play with

box: Nouns name the game and the tool: ball, rope, chalk, swing.
Verbs tell the action: throw, jump, skip, play.

mini: Draw and label one game and its tool.

sit.t: Break time. Some pupils play outside, some play inside the classroom because it is raining.
q: Which games do you play outside?
Which games do you play inside?

read.task: Read the word. Then show how you play with it.

write.task: Write: "ball", "rope", "skip". Then write one sentence: "I like ____."

integ: Tell your friend your favourite game and its tool: "I like skipping. I use a rope."
rubric: name five games and their tools
say what I do with a ball and a rope
label a drawing of a game

title: Playing Together and Giving Instructions
comp: give and follow simple instructions when we play

box: An instruction starts with a verb: Throw the ball. Jump now.
We use then for the next action: Sit, then stand.

phon.focus: Final sounds in game and action words

mini: Add one instruction or game-related request to the strip.

sit.t: You are the captain of your team. Your friends do not know the game. You must explain it.
q: What do you say first?
How do you explain the next action?

read.task: Read the instruction. Then do it.

write.task: Write two instructions for a game. Use and or then.

integ: Be the captain. Give three instructions. Your team follows them correctly.
rubric: give three clear play instructions
use and and then
follow my friend's instructions

title: Playing Safely and Using Polite Words
comp: use polite words and rules so that everybody plays safely

box: Can I join? May I use the chalk?
Polite questions end with a question mark.

phon.focus: Digraphs in polite and play words

mini: Add a polite request or a rule to the strip.

sit.t: Two pupils are playing with the only rope. You also want to play, but you must ask politely.
q: What do you say to them?
What rules keep the game safe?

read.task: Read each rule. Then say if it is polite or not.

write.task: Write two polite sentences for the playground.

l: Bih: Can I join your game?
Ngo: Yes, you can. Wait your turn.
Bih: May I use the rope first?

integ: Act the dialogue. Then make one rule for your class playground and say it politely.
rubric: ask to join a game politely
say three rules for safe play
read and spell chalk, shout, chair

title: Describing Favorite Games and Final Presentation
comp: describe my favourite game and present my work

box: she like jump → She likes to jump. he play game → He plays a fun game.
Add -s with he, she, it.

mini: Finalise the strip with drawings, instructions and a chant.

sit.t: Your teacher asks: "What is your favourite game, and why?"
q: What is your favourite game?
Who do you play it with?

read.task: Read the sentences. Then say which game you like.

write.task: Write three sentences about your favourite game. Correct "she like jump" first.

l: This is my game. (show the strip)
I jump the rope with my friend. (jump)
We play fair and we are polite. (smile)

integ: Present your strip and teach the class one game in English, using instructions.
rubric: describe my favourite game
correct a sentence with the verb -s
present my My Game Strip and teach a game

title: Naming Communication Forms and Tools
comp: name the ways and tools we use to send messages

box: Nouns name the tools: phone, letter, radio, drum.
Pronouns replace names: She calls. He writes. I talk.

mini: Draw and label one form of communication (phone, letter or speech).

sit.t: Your father is in Douala. You want to tell him about your school prize.
q: How can you send him a message?
What do you say to him?

read.task: Read the word. Then say how you use it.

write.task: Write: "She calls." "He writes." Then label your drawing.

integ: Show three ways to send a message without words: a wave, a smile, a drum. Say what each one means.
rubric: name four communication tools
say how I send a message
label a drawing of a communication tool

title: Expressing Feelings and Ideas
comp: say how I feel and how other people feel

box: Interjections show feeling: Oh! Wow! Sorry!
Adjectives tell how somebody is: happy, sad, kind, calm.

mini: Add one feeling or expression phrase to the strip.

sit.t: Your friend lost her pen. She is looking at the ground and she is quiet.
q: How does she feel?
What do you say to her?

read.task: Read the sentence. Then show the feeling on your face.

write.task: Write two sentences: "I am ____ today." "My friend is ____."

integ: Make a feelings face. Your friend looks at it and says: "You are happy!" or "You are sad."
rubric: say how I feel
describe how a friend feels
use Wow!, Oh! and Sorry! correctly

title: Asking and Answering Questions Politely
comp: ask and answer questions clearly and politely

gram.focus: Question words who, what, where; punctuation
box: We ask with Who…? What…? Where…?
Every question ends with a question mark (?).

phon.focus: Digraphs in question and answer words

mini: Add a question or an answer sentence to the strip.

sit.t: A new pupil comes into your class. She does not know anybody.
q: What do you ask her?
How do you answer her questions?

i: Who are you? I am Sam.
What is this? It is a book.
Where is the teacher? He is in the class.
read.task: Read the question, then read the answer.

write.task: Write two questions and two answers. Remember the question mark.

l: Ngo: My name is Ngo. Who are you?
Bih: I am Bih. Where do you live?
Ngo: I live near the school.

integ: Interview a friend with three questions. Then tell the class about your friend.
rubric: ask questions with who, what, where
answer questions in a full sentence
read and spell what, she, where

title: Sharing Messages and Final Presentation
comp: give a simple message clearly and present my communication strip

gram.focus: Editing messages; review of sentence types and punctuation
box: she call him → She called him. they write letter → They write a letter.
Check: capital letter, verb, full stop or question mark.

mini: Finalise and present the communication strip with tools, phrases and a chant.

sit.t: You must take a message to your neighbour: his son is coming home today.
q: What is your message?
How do you say it politely?

read.task: Read the message. Then say who it is for.

write.task: Write a short message to a friend. Correct "they write letter" first.

l: This is a phone. I call my father. (show the strip)
This is a letter. I write a message. (write motion)
Talk with care and be polite. (smile)

integ: Present your strip to the class. Give your message clearly, then answer two questions.
rubric: give a message clearly
correct a message sentence
present my How We Communicate Strip
